rows.title: Beginning Classical Guitar

rows.title: Principles of Nursing Practice and Simple Concepts
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Communication: The student nurse will identify communication skills to support decision making, education, and documentation of care related to principles of nursing and simple concepts.

Thinking & Reasoning: The student nurse will identify the steps of the nursing process and best current evidence to provide safe care related to principles of nursing and simple concepts while advocating for patients and families across the lifespan.
Information Management: The student nurse will identify technology to support decision making, education, and documentation of care related to principles of nursing and simple concepts.
Diversity: The student will recognize individual responsibility, personal integrity, and respect for culturally diverse patient populations.
Civic Responsibility: The student nurse will identify responsibility for becoming informed, ethical and active nurses in their community.
Life Skills: The student nurse will identify interpersonal skills while providing safe care related to principles of nursing and simple concepts.
Careers: The student nurse will evaluate accountability and responsibility for nursing practice, employing professionalism in the role of the registered nurse.

rows.title: Role Transition
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Communication & Information Management By the end of the course, the student will differentiate between verbal and written therapeutic and non-therapeutic communication skills.

Thinking/Reasoning & Life Skills: By the end of the course, the student will demonstrate the ability to analyze the nursing process related to delivery of safe nursing care through the development of a concept map.

Careers, Civic Responsibility & Diversity: By the end of the course, the student will be able to define the role and responsibility of the professional nurse in the diverse healthcare population as defined by the California Nurse Practice Act and Standards of Nursing Practice.

rows.title: Complex Concepts and Preceptorship Lab
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Communication: The graduate nurse will synthesize communication skills to support decision making, education, and documentation of care related to concepts of leadership.

Thinking & Reasoning: The graduate nurse will differentiate the nursing process and best current evidence to provide safe care related to concepts of leadership while advocating for patients and families across the lifespan.
Information Management: The graduate nurse will synthesize the use of technology to support decision making, education, and documentation of care related to concepts of leadership.
Diversity: The graduate nurse will internalize individual responsibility, personal integrity, and respect for culturally diverse patient populations.
Civic Responsibility: The graduate nurse will internalize the responsibilities for becoming informed, ethical and active nurses in their community.
Life Skills: The graduate nurse will internalize the application of interpersonal skills while providing safe care related to complex concepts.
Careers: The graduate nurse will internalize the accountability and responsibility for nursing practice, employing professionalism in the role of the Registered Nurse.

rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Civic Participation - Students will demonstrate a general understanding of the theoretical foundations of the American political system and its emphasis on liberty, equality, sovereignty, and deliberation.
Thinking and Reasoning - Students will evaluate the democratic nature of American governmental institutions using standards of popular sovereignty, political equality, and liberty.

Diversity - Students will identify and explain contrasting views on the role of government, the virtues and vices of democratic decision making, and the balance of executive, legislative, and judicial power.

rows.title: Concepts in Physical Sciences for Educators
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Identify a physical science principle and apply the principle to a given question or problem.
Use the scientific method in problem solving by first predicting an outcome and then completing an experiment.
Use logical reasoning in interpreting the data from experiments.
Collaborate on guided-inquiry labs in small learning communities thus developing skills to interact with others from different backgrounds, perspective and ideas.
Apply learned physical science concepts to a broader global perspective of current events.

rows.title: Introduction to Child Psychology
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate familiarity with major child developmental concepts, methods of study, and theories.
Identify and understand each developmental stage in the context of  the major developmental theories.
Demonstrate familiarity with social and cultural differences in child development as it relates to major developmental themes and practices.

rows.title: Introduction to Biological Psychology
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Explain the synaptic process as it relates to normal and abnormal (i.e., drug effects and mental disorders) functions.
Explain the etiology, course, and treatment of mental disorders utilizing biological concepts.
Identify various molar and molecular structures of the CNS, including corresponding functions.
Apply knowledge of mental processes using neurophysiological and neuroanatomical concepts, principles, and theories
Demonstrate familiarity with the behavioral methods used to study brain-behavior relationships

Locate the fundamental structural components of the neuron and demonstrate knowledge of neural communication, emphasizing resting potential, action potential, depolarization, hyperpolarization, metabotropic receptors, ionotropic receptors, and synaptic transmission.
Distinguish the functions of the fundamental structures of the nervous system, emphasizing major divisions of the brain

rows.title: Introduction to Social Psychology
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Analyze the findings of, and possible ethical issues associated with, classic experiments conducted in the field of social psychology (i.e., Stanford prison experiment, Milgram’s obedience study, Asch’s conformity study).
Analyze cognitive biases and norm violations in everyday, social situations.
Evaluate the ethical considerations of the psychological research methodology used in the field (e.g., deception, psychological harm).

rows.title: Psychology and Law
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Apply psychological theories and law research to real-world legal contexts.
Identify how experimental findings and social psychology concepts inform and influence decision-making, attitudes, and behaviors in the context of the legal system.
Evaluate the ways that psychologists interact with the legal system and can inform legal proceedings (e.g., insanity defense, competency)

rows.title: Introduction to Phonetics
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Differentiate consonants by manner, place, and voicing and vowels by position of front, central, and back.
Transcribe words and sentences using the International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA) in broad transcription.

rows.title: Social Problems
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Students will be able to identify and analyze how sociological principles, concepts, and categories (e.g. age, gender, class, race, ethnicity, sexual orientation, etc.) are applied in the understanding of social problems.
Students will determine the causes and the extent of social trends and problems such as racial discrimination, poverty, social violence, immigration, gender inequality, and crime.

Students will identify and explain the extent and consequences of current social issues and problems in the US and globally through the interpretation of data describing social changes in the areas of family, work, school, religion, and/or the economy.

rows.title: Introduction to LGBTQ+ Studies
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate familiarity with the major concepts, theories, methods and findings in LGBTQ+ studies.
Apply the major sociological theories and perspectives to the issues and experiences within LGBTQ+ studies.

rows.title: Elementary Spanish II
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Use appropriate grammatical structures that include advanced vocabulary, verb conjugations, and regional usage of common lexicon.
Write more complex paragraphs, dialogues, and compositions with an enhanced level of appropriate syntax and grammar.
Read, analyze, and express personal opinions in Spanish on a diverse set of cultural topics.
Engage in oral discussions by actively listening and speaking on a variety of topics related to the Spanish-speaking world.

rows.title: Intermediate Spanish I
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Write multiple compositions in Spanish at the intermediate level using description, summary, comparisons, and other modes.
Demonstrate understanding of critical analysis of literary material.
Express personal opinions and perspectives in Spanish on specific readings.
Engage in oral discussions by actively listening and speaking on topics related to cultural aspects of the Spanish-speaking world.

rows.title: College Business Spanish
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Communicate effectively in Spanish at the Intermediate level while using appropriate business vocabulary and applying grammatical structures correctly.
Outline and complete short writing assignments such as business letters and reports.
Analyze different ways to use business Spanish vocabulary in different Spanish-speaking countries.
Review library resources and web for Spanish material focusing in investments, banking, and management.

rows.title: Introduction to Statistics - Honors
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: PART 2:
Correctly interpret a graphical display of data.
Take a statistical claim about a data set, perform an appropriate procedure, and write a conclusion that addresses that claim.

rows.title: Acting Fundamentals
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Compare basic acting skills, including physical, vocal, imaginative, analytical, and emotional elements.
Evaluate the strengths and weaknesses of a scene performance.
Select objectives, obstacles, and tactics for performance.

rows.title: Introduction to Technical Theatre
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Recognize technical theater equipment.
Employ technical theater design methods.
Generate technical theater drawings and related paperwork.

rows.title: Introduction to Sound Design
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Apply the steps in creating a sound design for a theatrical script.
Create sound plots, cue sheets, and system paperwork required for a theatrical event.
Employ the safe operation of sound equipment and tools, inlcuding recording, editing, and cue playback.

rows.title: Lighting Fundamentals
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding a stage light plot.
Create supporting paperwork for a lighting design.
Interpret scripts for technical lighting components through written analysis.

rows.title: Costume Periods and Styles
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Analyze changes in the historical silhouette over time.
Discuss the variety of forces influencing costume choices including protection, social, political, religious, and decorative.
Distinguish between secondary and primary sources of documentation and explain the relative importance of each.

rows.title: Showcase I
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Gain practical experience in using their imaginations to develop character interpretations.
Evaluate their own acting skills based on the critique and support that they have received during class.
Participate in ensemble acting assignments to recognize the importance of both collaboration and diversity in seeking common solutions to acting tasks.

rows.title: Children's Theatre Ensemble
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate original thought by using their imaginations when developing character choices for performance.
Use imagination and personal interpretation in the development of their characters.
Identify, interpret, define, develop, and utilize character objectives, obstacles, and tactics when developing character choices.

rows.title: Principles of Playwriting
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Compare and create situation versus incident, as well as, differentiate through application of principles of selectivity and heightening what is stage truth versus life truth.
Formulate basic plot proportions from full length to one act plays.
Examine and formulate ideas for plays from thematic, situational and character sources, as well as, distinguish and assemble primary elements of plot structure.

rows.title: Intermediate Musical Theatre Workshop
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Compare and contrast musical theatre performance techniques.
Comprehend the audition, rehearsal, and performance process for a professional musical theatre production.
Participate in an ensemble musical performance demonstrating articulation skills, analytical skills, physical flexibility, dance steps, vocal techniques, and personal confidence.

rows.title: Introduction to Automotive
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate the ability to perform a vehicle safety inspection.
Explain the importance of automotive certifications for employment in an automotive service and repair facility as a technician.
Describe the function and operation of the powertrain and drivetrain systems found on modern automobiles.

rows.title: Automatic and Manual Transmissions & Transaxles
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Identify five major components of an automatic transmission.
Identify five major components of a manual transmission.
Demonstrate proper disassembly and reassembly of a transmission.
Demonstrate disassembly and reassembly of a rear wheel drive differential unit.
Analyze automatic transmission fluid for abnormal color, smell, and texture to determine fluid quality.

rows.title: Microsoft Windows Overview
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Know how to and where to save files and create folders in specific drives.
Use the desktop and name some of its common features (e.g., icons, start button, program windows, and taskbar).
Minimize, maximize, restore down, and close a window.

rows.title: Practical Computer & Internet Skills for Parents & Guardians
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Implement at least one way to increase internet safety for children.
Use at least one online resource (student information system, learning management system, district website, educational tools, etc.) to help their child succeeed in school.

rows.title: Navigating the Internet
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Prepare a simple web-based search.
Implement ways to increase internet safety.
Locate and choose an internet browser to load a webpage and view it.

rows.title: Introduction to Microsoft Outlook
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Manage contacts by creating distribution lists.
Organize emails by creating a filter to transfer emails to a specific folder.
Identify and avoid opening emails and attachments that are suspicious.
Schedule a meeting request in the Outlook calendar.

rows.title: Global Business Professional (CGBP) Certification Exam Preparation  & Practice
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Prepare for the latest Global Business Professional (CGBP) certification exam.

rows.title: Human Resources Compliance
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Interpret and apply employment laws and regulations in HR decision-making and organizational compliance.
Examine key principles and best practices in labor and employee relations
Analyze and address potential workplace risks through proactive mitigation strategies.

rows.title: Employability Skills
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Complete a career assessment to identify careers that best match their skills, abilities, talents, and interests.
Connect with others by being a good listener, asking questions to help understand what the other person is feeling, and mirroring positive nonverbal communication to build trust.
Answer interview questions honestly and thoroughly.

rows.title: Digital Literacy for Academic and Professional Success - Tier 2
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Identify and apply proper etiquette for social media and professionalism.
Evaluate different websites.
Utilize a learning management system.

rows.title: Information Technology (IT) Basics Tier 2
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Describe the difference between a cloud based system versus a server based network system.
Design and develop steps for troubleshooting computer programs.
Create a technical diagram of a cloud based system.

rows.title: Vocational Construction Technology Module I
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Perform first aid and CPR.
Follow OSHA standards when preparing tools and/or equipment.
Use tools properly and safely.

rows.title: Introduction to Drone Pilot Training
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate basic flight operations of a drone.
Perform mission-specific tasks involving aerial photography and video.
Perform basic safety and emergency procedures for fly aways, loss of control link, and other inflight incidents.

rows.title: Line Cook Training
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: List and explain all basics in regard to heat application as to: roasting, sauteing, pan frying, braising, simmering, deep frying, submerge poaching, and shallow poaching.
Define proper methods and techniques when applying all basic fundamental standards of cooking.
Identify basic kitchen utensils and equipment associated with the culinary profession, as well as measuring devices.
List and explain all basics in regard to heat application as to: roasting, sauteing, pan frying, braising, simmering, deep frying, submerge poaching, and shallow poaching.
Define proper methods and techniques when applying all basic fundamental standards of cooking.
Identify basic kitchen utensils and equipment associated with the culinary profession, as well as measuring devices.

rows.title: Introduction to Cakes and Decorating
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Produce and assemble assorted classical and contemporary cakes and tortes which meet quality standards.
Discuss and apply correct mixing methods for a variety of buttercreams, icings, fondants, glazes and meringues.
Demonstrate profiency in piping various icings.
Describe and apply correct procedures for icing/finishing cakes and tortes, including a variety of specific decorating techniques.

rows.title: Commercial Dance II
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Memorize and identify dance vocabulary appropriate to level II commercial dance to recognize and interpret verbal and written instruction.
Demonstrate technical skills and expressive performance skills appropriate to level II commercial dance.
Utilize critical writing skills to self-assess strengths and weaknesses in level II commercial dance.
Demonstrate appropriate preparations for a mock dance audition setting.

rows.title: Technical Theatre in Production
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Evaluate varied control and operational techniques.
Correct problems for non-responsive or non-working technical components.
Apply effective methods to meet the technical demands of back stage operations.

rows.title: Ballet II
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Memorize and identify ballet dance vocabulary appropriate to level II to recognize and interpret verbal and written instruction.
Demonstrate technical skills and expressive performance skills appropriate to ballet dance level II.
Use critical writing skills to analyze and criticize one’s own technical skills and expressive performance skills appropriate to ballet dance level II.
Use critical writing skills to complete personal critique and reflection of a ballet dance concert performance.
Discuss and interpret elements of dance composition appropriate to ballet dance level II.

rows.title: Jazz Dance I
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Memorize and identify ballet and jazz dance vocabulary appropriate to level I to recognize and interpret verbal and written instruction.
Demonstrate technical skills and expressive performance skills appropriate to jazz dance level I.
Use critical writing skills to analyze and criticize one’s own technical skills and expressive performance skills appropriate to jazz dance level I.
Use critical writing skills to complete personal critique and reflection of a jazz dance concert performance.
Discuss and interpret elements of dance composition appropriate to jazz dance level I.

rows.title: Hip-Hop Dance I
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Memorize and identify hip-hop dance vocabulary appropriate to level I to recognize and interpret verbal and written instruction.
Demonstrate technical skills and expressive performance skills appropriate to hip-hop dance level I.
Use critical writing skills to complete personal critique and reflection of a hip-hop dance performance.
Discuss and interpret elements of dance composition appropriate to hip-hop dance level I.

rows.title: Certified Nursing Assistant (CNA) Training - Theory
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Identify the roles and responsibilities of a CNA.
Demonstrate effective interpersonal communication skills for basic nursing care, and a positive working relationship with all members of the healthcare team, residents and their families.
Identify the basic rules of safety, body mechanics, and patient positioning.
Identify standard precautions and basic principles related to medical and surgical asepsis.
Identify metric system, weights, and military time.
Demonstrate ability to care for patients including bathing, dressing, overall hygiene, feeding and toileting.
Accurately measure and record vital signs, height, weight and state normal parameters of each.
Demonstrate ability to recognize and report patient abuse.
Identify the concepts of Patient’s and Resident’s Rights.

rows.title: Acute Care Nursing Assistant Theory
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Describe and implement proper care for patients in acute care setting.
Exhibit proficient communication, interpersonal, and documentation abilities to enhance patient care.
Collaborate with licensed nursing staff to assess and monitor patients in an acute care setting, providing valuable support in the healthcare team.

rows.title: Personal Caregiver/Care Aide-Skills Lab
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Perform correct hand hygiene, PPE use, and infection control techniques.
Safely assist clients with transfers, ambulation, and positioning.
Provide ADLs, nutrition assistance, and basic household care in a safe and dignified manner.

rows.title: Introduction to Biotechnology
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Have a fundamental overview of the applications and underlying principles of biotechnology.

rows.title: Elementary Vietnamese I
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Write basic descriptive paragraphs in Vietnamese with clear topic sentences and supporting detail.
Internalize the sound system, basic tones, and structure of the Vietnamese language.
Read, analyze, and express personal opinions in Vietnamese on a diverse set of cultural topics.
Use appropriate grammatical structures that include beginning-level vocabulary and verb markers.
Engage in oral discussions by actively listening and speaking on a variety of topics.

rows.title: Intermediate Electric Arc Welding
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate safety standards and rules given in this course that apply to welding equipment, work habits, and industrial environment.
Recognize the electrode classification system.
Differentiate between common electrodes and their uses.

rows.title: Pipe Welding Fundamentals
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate safety standards and rules given in this course that apply to welding equipment, work habits, and industrial environment.
Recognize the electrode classification system used in pipe welding.
Perform pipe welding techniques in the 1G and 2G positions.

rows.title: Structural Welding SMAW
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate safety standards and rules given in this course that apply to welding equipment, work habits, and industrial environment.
Create welds in the vertical (3G) and overhead (4G) positions using the Shielded Metal Arc Welding (SMAW) process.
Reconstruct an AWS D1.1 unlimited thickness test plate.

rows.title: Advanced Pipe Welding
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate safety standards and rules given in this course that apply to welding equipment, work habits, and industrial environment.
Recognize 6G testing procedures stated in the American Petroleum Institute standard 1104.
Identify different destructive and non-destructive testing methods for pipe welding in accordance to the American Petroleum Institute standard 1104.
